LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.5: Money
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money, part of Measurement in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: how to represent same amount How do you represent the same amount of money using different denominations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to Kenyan currency.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: Learners develop communication skills as they communicate and collaborate with their peers, in pairs or in groups

counting Kenyan currency notes in different denominations up to sh1000 using imitation money.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: Evaluation and decision making is developed as the learner role plays by buying up to 3 items

involving balance using real or imitation money up to sh.1000 in shopping activities.

Values:
Patriotism: Learners dedicate while working in pairs or groups sort out Kenyan currency notes according to their value up to sh.1000.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy: The choice of what to buy and what not to buy as learners in groups role play buying up to 3 items involving

balance using imitation money up to sh.1000 in shopping activities.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills used in modelling the Kenyan currency denominations to modelling skills in Creative Activities.

Suggested Learning resources:

Kenyan currency coins and notes or imitations up to sh.1000, classroom shop, digital devices
